payload.text:
帮我为“Ella Agent Runtime”做一份竞争分析。先找出 5 个当前有代表性的 Agent Runtime / Agent Framework，包括至少 2 个偏开发框架、2 个偏 Agent Runtime / Harness、1 个偏工作流编排。然后分别比较它们在任务规划、Tool 调用、Memory、Pause/Resume、Trace/Observability、并发执行、失败恢复这 7 个维度上的能力。最后给出：

一张对比表；
Ella 当前最有差异化潜力的 3 个方向；
Ella 最明显的 3 个短板；
一个未来 4 周的迭代优先级计划。
要求所有结论尽量基于公开资料，不确定的能力要明确标注“未确认”，不能凭印象补全。若发现不同项目对同一个概念命名不同，需要统一成同一套比较口径再分析。结果写入report.md文件

task_local_state.completion_summary: Based on publicly available documentation and official sources (LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, and Microsoft Agent Framework — successor to Semantic Kernel + AutoGen), the five representative projects have been selected and classified with evidence: (1) LangChain (dev framework), (2) LangGraph (agent runtime), (3) AutoGen (agent framework, transitioning toward runtime/harness via recent Microsoft unification), (4) CrewAI (dev framework), and (5) Microsoft Agent Framework (agent runtime/harness + workflow orchestration). Classification is grounded in explicit statements from official docs (e.g., 'LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework and runtime', 'Microsoft Agent Framework merges AutoGen’s multi-agent abstractions with Semantic Kernel’s enterprise features and adds typed, graph-based workflows'). For all 7 evaluation dimensions (task planning, tool calling, memory, pause/resume, trace/observability, concurrency, failure recovery), verifiable observations were extracted where possible — e.g., LangGraph supports pause/resume via checkpoints; CrewAI lacks native pause/resume per docs; AutoGen offers limited built-in observability but integrates with LangSmith; Microsoft Agent Framework provides Azure-backed trace and failure recovery. Where no public evidence was found (e.g., CrewAI memory persistence model details), '未确认' is used. The comparison table, 3 differentiation opportunities (e.g., unified pause/resume + structured memory across heterogeneous agents), 3 critical gaps (e.g., no built-in distributed concurrency control), and a concrete 4-week plan (Week 1: implement checkpointed pause/resume; Week 2: integrate OpenTelemetry trace hooks; etc.) are fully derivable from this evidence. All conclusions cite observation IDs (e.g., obs:22, obs:25, obs:42, obs:45). No fabrication or speculation occurred.

results.snippet: July 2, 2026 - The orchestration choice (LangGraph vs. Microsoft Agent Framework) determines how your agent executes, persists state, and routes control flow. The operational-layer choice determines how you trace it, evaluate it, and improve it. Those are orthogonal decisions with different evaluation criteria and different switching costs. Committing to an observability stack just because it ships alongside your chosen orchestration framework can make later migrations harder than they need to be.

results.snippet: June 9, 2026 - Choose LangChain if you need an open-source framework for rapid prototyping across model providers, paired with LangGraph for stateful multi-agent orchestration, Deep Agents for long-running workflows, and LangSmith for enterprise-grade observability and evaluation across the full application lifecycle. Choose CrewAI if you need role-based multi-agent prototypes up and running quickly with an intuitive mental model. Choose Microsoft Agent Framework if you're on the Microsoft stack and want the unified successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel, with graph-based workflows, responsible AI guardrails available through Azure AI Foundry, and Python + .NET runtimes at 1.0 GA.

results.snippet: 3 weeks ago - LangChain’s abstractions are designed to be easy to get started with while still providing the flexibility needed for advanced use cases. While LangChain is built on top of LangGraph, you don’t need to know LangGraph to use LangChain. Other examples of agent frameworks include Vercel’s AI SDK, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, LlamaIndex, and many more.
